author: kenji_rag_lead
title: Unbeatable structural integrity and zero 404 image links
body: We tested reference-native on our internal knowledge base of 40,000 enterprise Word and Visio files. The kebab-case semantic image extraction linked directly inside Markdown eliminated missing figure hallucinations completely in GPT-4o.

author: sarah_cloud_ops
title: Sub-10ms latency without GPU instances
body: Runs entirely on CPU in standard Docker containers without any heavy PyTorch dependencies. Memory footprint hovered below 200MB during sustained batch runs.

author: alex_nlp_research
title: Superb table understanding, but resource-heavy
body: Docling reconstructs nested PDF tables exceptionally well. However, CPU processing takes around 400-600ms per page, which requires clustering when running on 100k+ documents.

author: t_yamamoto_dev
title: Lightweight and easy to integrate, struggles with merged cells
body: MarkItDown is our go-to for lightweight automated ingestion in small pipelines. It occasionally drops multi-column table headers, but setup is virtually zero-effort.

author: david_enterprise_arch
title: Solid all-rounder for enterprise connectors
body: Broad file support across legacy formats. Token density is slightly elevated due to boilerplate tags, but very dependable across legacy document dumps.

author: mika_ai_engineer
title: High accuracy on complex layouts, cloud-dependency is a trade-off
body: Excels on dense scanned forms and financial tables. Ingestion costs scale up with volume, so evaluate ROI for high-throughput batch pipelines.
